stories.title: UK to introduce mandatory supply chain human rights law
stories.summary: The UK government announced a new mandatory human rights due diligence regime for large businesses. Companies with over £350 million in revenue must monitor and address forced labor risks across their supply chains. The government says the law targets businesses with the capability to manage these risks.

stories.title: Asia Pacific leads in sustainability reporting
stories.summary: Research by ACCA suggests Asia Pacific is a global leader in adopting sustainability reporting standards. The report notes that over 80% of ASEAN economies by GDP have adopted or plan to adopt standards from the International Sustainability Standards Board. Policymakers are now encouraged to move beyond mere compliance.

stories.title: SINBON Electronics links executive pay to ESG
stories.summary: SINBON Electronics released its 2025 Sustainability Report, highlighting institutionalized governance and a living wage survey. The company says sustainability is a core driver of corporate competitiveness. It continues to meet global supply chain expectations by delivering low-carbon solutions and co-creating value with its diverse stakeholders.

stories.title: Mankind Pharma receives independent ESG rating
stories.summary: SES ESG Research assigned Mankind Pharma an ESG rating of 64.8 for FY26. The rating was based solely on publicly available information. The company disclosed the result under SEBI listing regulations, noting that the assessment was conducted independently without any engagement or commission from the firm.

stories.title: Indo Count ESG score climbs to 78
stories.summary: Indo Count reported an S&P Global ESG score of 78 out of 100, up from 45 over two years. The company claims this is 47 points above the industry average of 31. It also reported 30,000 metric tons of greenhouse-gas reductions through its Project Gigaton.

stories.title: NTPC ESG rating rises to 64.2
stories.summary: NTPC received an updated ESG rating of 64.2 from SES ESG Research, an improvement of 1.4 points. The assessment was based entirely on publicly available information and conducted independently. The company did not engage the agency for the evaluation.

stories.title: Tamilnad Mercantile Bank files sustainability report
stories.summary: Tamilnad Mercantile Bank filed its Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report for FY 2025-26. The bank reported improved operational efficiency metrics and material business risks. It also disclosed monetary penalties totaling ₹45,03,750 imposed by various regulatory bodies during the financial year.

stories.title: FCA sets path for ESG ratings regulation
stories.summary: The UK financial regulator has confirmed plans to bring providers of company ESG ratings within its scope. The process is expected to take place over the next two years. The regulator has described the move as a sensible evolution.

stories.title: Apollo Tyres appoints chief sustainability officer
stories.summary: Apollo Tyres has appointed Rajeev Kumar Sinha as Whole-Time Director and Chief Manufacturing and Sustainability Officer. The company also assigned an ESG rating of 71 for FY25 and FY26. Shareholders are currently voting on the appointment via a postal ballot.

stories.title: Indian Oil Corporation files sustainability report
stories.summary: Indian Oil Corporation filed its BRSR for FY 2025-26, reporting energy savings of 4,14,126 SRFT per year. The company claims the highest rank in the Indian oil and gas sector on the 2025 Dow Jones Sustainability Index. It reported nil monetary penalties across all NGRBC principles.

stories.title: Expleo Solutions reports zero safety incidents
stories.summary: Expleo Solutions submitted its BRSR for FY 2025-26, reporting a total workforce of 4,177 employees. The company recorded zero safety incidents, zero monetary penalties, and zero data breaches. It also received a Corporate Excellence Award for space optimization.

stories.title: Axis Bank files sustainability report
stories.summary: Axis Bank filed its Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report for FY 2025-26. The report details a workforce of over 1.11 lakh employees with 30.1% female representation. The bank also addressed nearly 5 lakh customer complaints and invested ₹102.33 crore in CSR initiatives.

stories.title: India secures $400 billion in renewable commitments
stories.summary: India has secured long-term renewable energy investment commitments of approximately $400 billion. Minister Pralhad Joshi said ₹7 trillion has already flowed into the sector over two years. He expressed confidence that an additional ₹21 trillion required by 2030 would materialize to support 500 gigawatts of capacity.

stories.title: Senate reviews carbon credit legislation
stories.summary: The Senate has referred the Carbon Credits and Other Legislation Amendment Bill 2026 to a standing committee. The bill proposes amendments to existing carbon credit frameworks. The Environmental Defenders Office has provided a submission on the bill, noting it does not constitute professional legal advice.

stories.title: Green Genius raises $72.5 million in green bonds
stories.summary: Renewable energy developer Green Genius has completed a €65 million green bond issue. The bonds carry a floating interest rate based on the EURIBOR plus 8% annually. The company says the funds will be used to refinance existing subordinated construction loans.

stories.title: Climate policy progress slows
stories.summary: Global climate policy progress has slowed, making emissions targets increasingly difficult to reach. The latest assessment from Sustainable Views indicates that the pace of international policy development is falling behind established climate goals.

stories.title: Isometric launches CBAM preparation service
stories.summary: Isometric has launched a service to help cement exporters prepare emissions data for the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism. The company says it helps exporters address findings from verifiers, though it does not perform the formal verification itself. Cementir is already using the platform.

stories.title: COP31 event examines transition carbon credits
stories.summary: A COP31 side event is discussing whether transition carbon credits can accelerate decarbonization in Southeast Asia. The full piece is for subscribers. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: Isometric launches CBAM reporting service
stories.summary: Isometric has launched Ready for CBAM, a service designed to help exporters prepare emissions data for the EU carbon tax. The mechanism aims to prevent carbon leakage by equalizing prices for imported goods. The EU adopted the policy in 2023 and it entered force this year.

stories.title: BBVA issues green bonds
stories.summary: BBVA has placed 390 million Swiss francs in a two-tranche senior preferred green bond issuance. The full details of the transaction are available to subscribers of the source publication. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: BRAC Bank to issue green bond
stories.summary: BRAC Bank will launch a 1,000 crore taka green bond on 15 November to fund sustainable projects in Bangladesh. The three-year bond has a face value of 10 lakh taka and is open to both corporate and individual investors. The bank calls this an important milestone.

stories.title: COP30 presidency outlines transition roadmaps
stories.summary: Brazil’s outgoing COP30 presidency has released roadmaps for fossil fuel transitions and forest finance. The plan suggests countries replace fossil fuels between 2031 and 2033. The presidency says governments must act rather than renegotiate, though no enforcement mechanism was reported for the proposed timeline.

stories.title: Carbon Gap releases removal toolkit
stories.summary: Carbon Gap has launched a free, open-access toolkit for estimating a country's carbon dioxide removal potential. The methodology was refined over two years and applied in seven countries. The group plans to present the tool to national delegations at the upcoming COP31 summit.

stories.title: Webinar to address CBAM cost management
stories.summary: A webinar scheduled for 3 November will cover cost management and verification under the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism. Since January, importers must surrender certificates for embedded emissions. The cost of these certificates depends on whether a company uses verified actual values or default values.

stories.title: Debate continues on fossil-free zones
stories.summary: As delegates head to COP31, officials from Colombia and Vanuatu are advocating for the adoption of fossil-free zones. While nearly every country agreed to transition energy systems away from fossil fuels three years ago, there remains no agreement on how to start the process.

stories.title: COP31 BRIDGE initiative pilots five countries
stories.summary: Türkiye’s COP31 presidency has selected Ethiopia, Fiji, Indonesia, Pakistan, and Uzbekistan for its Climate Implementation Bridge initiative. The program promises to build finance-ready project portfolios and identify bottlenecks. The initiative aims to be judged by deals closed rather than plans written.

stories.title: COP31 agenda faces geopolitical distractions
stories.summary: COP31 in Antalya aims to be an implementation summit, though organizers acknowledge that world leaders are currently distracted by wars, protests, and elections. The event follows a year where conflict has disrupted global energy policy and climate action efforts.

stories.title: Experts frame COP31 as implementation test
stories.summary: Experts suggest the success of COP31 will depend on accountability and accessible financing rather than new promises. The summit, scheduled for 9-20 November in Antalya, is positioned by Türkiye as an implementation event intended to bridge the gap between existing climate commitments and tangible results.

stories.title: US lawmakers to attend COP31
stories.summary: A 19-member US congressional delegation plans to attend COP31 in Türkiye. The United States is not participating in negotiations following the withdrawal from the Paris Agreement, but lawmakers stated the delegation will perform an important diplomatic function during the summit.

stories.title: COP31 to focus on implementation
stories.summary: COP31 will convene in Antalya from 9 to 20 November to address the implementation of national climate pledges. With the 1.5-degree threshold expected to be exceeded, organizers state the conference must provide key impetus for emissions reductions and the consistent application of existing targets.

stories.title: UN publishes COP31 pavilion programme
stories.summary: The United Nations in Türkiye has released the schedule for side events at the COP31 Blue Zone pavilion. The space is intended to serve as a platform for dialogue between governments, the private sector, and civil society to advance climate action throughout the summit.

stories.title: Greenpeace MENA calls for energy transition
stories.summary: Greenpeace MENA has called for an accelerated energy transition ahead of COP31. The organization cites the high cost of fossil fuel dependence amid ongoing conflicts and food security pressures, noting that the region remains on the frontlines of these overlapping crises.

stories.title: EU heads to COP31 with clean energy goals
stories.summary: The EU is entering COP31 with goals for clean electrification and a firm stance on climate finance. Following a difficult COP30, the bloc is attempting a new approach to negotiations. It remains to be seen what the final deal will contain.

stories.title: COP31 seeks electrification agreement
stories.summary: COP31 aims to reach an agreement on electrification in a divided global climate. Further details regarding the summit's specific agenda and progress are available to subscribers of the source publication.

stories.title: COP31 faces affordability challenge
stories.summary: As COP31 approaches, representatives from over 190 countries are meeting against a backdrop of record heatwaves and floods. While clean energy technologies continue to advance, the summit aims to address the challenge of making these tools affordable for the millions who currently cannot access them.

stories.title: Volkswagen opens vehicle dismantling line in Zwickau
stories.summary: Volkswagen has opened an industrial dismantling line at its Zwickau plant to support material recovery and its after-sales business. The facility expects to process 4,100 vehicles annually starting in 2027, employing 100 people. The company describes the move as an expansion of its circular-economy capacity.

stories.title: Retailers discard up to 40% of returned goods
stories.summary: Half of retailers destroy or discard between 6% and 40% of returned items, according to research from ReBound Returns and Advanced Supply Chain. Only 27% of retailers divert most returns through circular routes. New EU regulations now ban the destruction of certain unsold consumer goods by large retailers.

stories.title: Somalia hosts first circular economy forum
stories.summary: Mogadishu hosted its first Circular Economy Forum to address the 2,000 tonnes of waste the city generates daily. Organized by Horn Thrive Hub, the event explored turning discarded materials into economic opportunities. The forum focused on strengthening recycling and reuse initiatives to create viable local businesses.

stories.title: Donegal community groups offered circular economy grants
stories.summary: Community groups in Donegal can apply for a share of 100,000 euro in funding through Circular.ie. Grants of 1,000, 5,000 and 10,000 euro are available for projects ranging from physical signage to website development. The fund aims to help circular initiatives reach a wider audience.

stories.title: India proposes allowing recycled plastic for food packaging
stories.summary: India is moving to allow recycled plastic in food packaging to help companies meet recycling targets. Under proposed FSSAI rules, recycled material must meet the same safety standards as new plastic, with safeguards against chemical contamination. The move aims to remove a regulatory hurdle for packaging makers.

stories.title: COP31 focuses on zero waste and circularity
stories.summary: COP31 in Antalya aims to be the conference of implementation, with the Turkish presidency highlighting waste and the circular economy as key pathways. Adviser Carlos Silva Filho wants these areas recognized in the final declaration. The event is scheduled to take place from 9 to 20 November.

stories.title: Wege Prize 2027 attracts 450 students
stories.summary: Ferris State University has opened the 14th cycle of its Wege Prize, drawing 450 students from 51 countries. The 90 teams are tasked with designing circular economy solutions for problems like water scarcity and construction waste. The competition follows a global shift from incubation to integration.

stories.title: Digital transformation and technology are driving the circular economy model.
stories.summary: Digital transformation and technology are driving the circular economy model. The limitations of the traditional linear economic model (extract - produce - discard) are becoming apparent as raw material costs and environmental pressures continue to rise. To sustain growth momentum, shifting to a circular economy

stories.title: Tata Power commissions 300 MW solar project
stories.summary: Tata Power has commissioned a 300 MW solar project in Karnataka for the Solar Energy Corporation of India. The facility is expected to produce 810 million units of electricity annually and prevent 103,820 tonnes of carbon emissions each year. The company's renewable portfolio has now reached 12 GW.

stories.title: Chalet Hotels targets net zero by 2040
stories.summary: Chalet Hotels has committed to net-zero greenhouse-gas emissions by 2040. The company reports that 61% of its electricity is currently sourced from renewables, a 16% increase over the previous fiscal year. It also operates a 100% electric guest fleet and nine LEED-certified assets.

stories.title: TWO WEEKS TO GO: Free masterclass on turning climate risk insights into adaptation action - edie
stories.summary: Measuring climate risk offers a snapshot of exposure, but rarely a shield against it. Boards understand the need for disclosure, what they often miss are the operational costs that persist long after the report is filed. stories.title: Endangered frogs return to the wild
stories.summary: Fifty-three southern giant burrowing frogs have been released into the wild following a rescue operation during the 2019-20 bushfires. Scientists collected 160 tadpoles from fire-affected areas in Victoria and raised them at Melbourne Zoo. The frogs were successfully bred in captivity for the first time last year.

stories.title: NLC India targets 50:50 energy mix by 2032
stories.summary: NLC India is working toward a 50:50 split between conventional and renewable energy by 2032. CMD Prasanna Kumar Acharya stated that an integrated approach combining thermal, renewable and storage capacity is essential to meet rising power demand. The company is currently pursuing a balanced growth strategy.

stories.title: NLC India plans renewable energy subsidiary IPO
stories.summary: NLC India plans to sell up to 10 crore shares in its renewable energy subsidiary, NLC India Renewables Limited, through an offer for sale ahead of a proposed IPO. The announcement follows a second quarter where the parent company saw its net profit more than double.

stories.title: Indus Towers reaches 50,000 solar site milestone
stories.summary: Indus Towers has deployed 50,000 solar powered telecom sites, which the company describes as creating a global benchmark for sustainable infrastructure at scale. It now aims to double that figure to 100,000 sites. The sun is being asked to power more infrastructure.

stories.title: Essar Renewables PPA details unavailable
stories.summary: The full details regarding the 300 MW renewable energy power purchase agreement between Essar Renewables and NHPC are currently unavailable due to a server error. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: Essar to invest 4,500 crore in renewable project
stories.summary: Essar plans to invest 4,500 crore into a 300 MW renewable energy project following a power purchase agreement with NHPC. Access to the specific details of the agreement is currently restricted by the host server.

stories.title: Essar signs 300 MW renewable energy agreement
stories.summary: Essar has signed a power purchase agreement with NHPC for a 300 MW renewable energy project. The company plans to invest 4,500 crore into the development. The agreement marks a significant addition to the company's renewable energy portfolio.

stories.title: Clean Max Enviro Energy Solutions issues green bond
stories.summary: Clean Max Enviro Energy Solutions has raised 2,500 crore through its first commercial and industrial green bond issuance. The company reported that its profit after tax climbed to 120 crore in the first half of the fiscal year, up from 19 crore previously.
